title: Graphs
summary: Plot points on the Cartesian plane, interpret and draw global graphs that describe real situations, and draw linear graphs from equations using a table of values.

notes.text: The **Cartesian plane** has a horizontal **$x$-axis** and a vertical **$y$-axis** that cross at the **origin** $(0;\ 0)$. Every point is described by an **ordered pair** $(x;\ y)$: first move along the $x$-axis (left or right), then along the $y$-axis (up or down). The axes divide the plane into four **quadrants**.

notes.caption: The Cartesian plane with quadrants I to IV (anticlockwise from top right) and the points A(3; 2), B(−2; 4), C(−4; −3) and D(2; −4). Each grid square is one unit.
Signs of the coordinates in each quadrant

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: The order matters: $(3;\ 2)$ and $(2;\ 3)$ are different points. Always go **across** ($x$) first, then **up or down** ($y$). A point with $x = 0$ lies on the $y$-axis, e.g. $(0;\ -5)$; a point with $y = 0$ lies on the $x$-axis.
A **global graph** shows the general shape of a relationship without exact values. It tells a story: how one quantity changes as another changes, often over time.

notes.caption: Describing global graphs
rows: The graph goes up from left to right: $y$ gets bigger as $x$ gets bigger
The graph goes down from left to right: $y$ gets smaller as $x$ gets bigger
The graph is horizontal: $y$ does not change
The graph is a straight line: $y$ changes at a constant rate
The graph is curved: the rate of change is not constant
The highest / lowest point of the graph
The points are joined, because every in-between value makes sense (time, temperature)
Separate points that are not joined (number of people, tickets sold)

notes.title: Worked example 1: reading a global graph
notes.problem: Describe Sipho's walk shown in the graph above.
steps: **A:** the distance increases at a constant rate: he walks away from home at a steady speed.
**B:** the graph is horizontal (constant): his distance from home does not change, so he has stopped, perhaps at a shop.
**C:** the distance increases again, and the graph is steeper than in A, so he walks further away, faster.
**D:** the distance decreases to zero: he walks back home. This section is less steep than C, so he is slower.
notes.answer: Walk away steadily, stop, walk further away faster, return home.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: On a distance-time graph, the **steeper** the line, the **faster** the movement. A horizontal line means no movement. Do not confuse the graph with a picture of the road: a graph going "down" means getting closer to home, not walking downhill.
An equation such as $y = 2x - 1$ gives a straight-line graph. To draw it:

items: Make a table of values: choose a few $x$-values (e.g. $-2$ to $3$) and calculate each $y$.
Plot each point $(x;\ y)$ on the Cartesian plane.
Join the points with a ruler and label the line with its equation.

notes.caption: The graph of y = 2x − 1 through the points in the table. It cuts the y-axis at (0; −1) and the x-axis at (½; 0).

notes.text: The **$y$-intercept** is where the graph cuts the $y$-axis: substitute $x = 0$. The **$x$-intercept** is where the graph cuts the $x$-axis: substitute $y = 0$ and solve.

notes.title: Worked example 3: is a point on the line?
notes.problem: Is the point $(-1;\ -4)$ on the line $y = 3x - 1$?
steps: This matches the $y$-value of the point.

items: A point is written $(x;\ y)$: across first, then up or down. Quadrants I to IV go anticlockwise from the top right.
Global graphs describe trends: increasing, decreasing, constant, linear or non-linear, maximum and minimum, continuous or discrete.
On a distance-time graph, steeper means faster and horizontal means stopped.
To draw a line from its equation, make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a ruler.
A point lies on a graph if its coordinates satisfy the equation.

questions.prompt: In which quadrant is the point $(-3;\ 4)$?
questions.explanation: $x$ is negative and $y$ is positive: the second quadrant (top left).

questions.prompt: The point $(2;\ 3)$ lies on the line $y = 2x - 1$.
In Sipho's distance-time graph in the notes, what does the horizontal section B show?
questions.explanation: His distance from home stays constant, so he is not moving.

questions.prompt: In Sipho's distance-time graph, in which section does he move fastest?
questions.explanation: C is the steepest section: the distance changes most in the least time.

questions.prompt: The graph of $y = x^2$ is a straight line.
questions.explanation: The values $x = 0;\ 1;\ 2;\ 3$ give $y = 0;\ 1;\ 4;\ 9$. The differences are not constant, so the graph is curved (non-linear).

A taxi leaves the rank, drives at a constant speed for 20 minutes, waits at a stop for 5 minutes, then drives back to the rank faster than before. Describe the shape of each part of the distance-from-rank against time graph.
questions.memo:
First part: straight line increasing (constant speed away) ✓ (1)
Second part: horizontal line (constant distance while waiting) ✓ (1)
Third part: straight line decreasing back to zero ✓ (1)
The third part is steeper than the first because the taxi is faster ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: Water in a kettle is at room temperature. It is heated until it boils at $100\ ^\circ\text{C}$, boils for a short while, and is then left to cool. Describe the global graph of temperature against time. Is the graph discrete or continuous?
questions.memo:
Increasing to a maximum of $100\ ^\circ\text{C}$ ✓ (1)
Constant (horizontal) while it boils, then decreasing (curving, slowing down) as it cools ✓ (1)
Continuous, because temperature and time have values in between ✓ (1)
